questions.question: Merchants and migrants first brought the teachings of the holy Quran to India in the ______ century.
questions.solution:
• Century: Seventh Century
  • Context: Arab traders brought Islam to the Malabar Coast (Kerala) through maritime trade routes.

questions.question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni was a contemporary of which Chola king?
questions.solution:
• Contemporary: Rajendra I
  • Conflict: Mahmud of Ghazni’s raids occurred during the peak of the Chola empire's power under Rajendra I.

questions.question: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim, Xuan Zang, came to the Indian subcontinent about _____ years ago.
questions.solution:
• Time: 1400 years ago (7th Century AD)
  • Visit: He visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana to study Buddhism.

questions.question: Vetti tax that is mentioned in the inscriptions of the Chola dynasty was taken in _____ form.
questions.solution:
• Nature: Forced labour
  • Detail: Unlike other taxes, Vetti was not paid in cash or kind but through manual labor for the state.

questions.question: Dadabhai Naoroji was a ______.
questions.solution:
• Profession: Businessman
  • Legacy: Known as the 'Grand Old Man of India', he was also a cotton trader and a professor before entering politics.

questions.question: Which of the following sequence is correct with respect to the Delhi Dynasties?
questions.option_1: Rajput dynasties, Khalji dynasty, Tughluq dynasty
questions.option_2: Tughluq dynasty, Khalji dynasty, Sayyid dynasty
questions.option_3: Early Turkish Rulers, Rajput dynasties, Khalji dynasty
questions.option_4: Khalji dynasty, Lodi dynasty, Sayyid dynasty
questions.solution:
• Correct Order: Rajputs > Khalji > Tughluq
  • Timeline: Tomars/Chauhans (12th C), Khaljis (1290–1320), Tughluqs (1320–1414).

questions.question: The first session of Indian National congress was held at ______.
questions.solution:
• City: Bombay (1885)
  • Venue: Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College; attended by 72 delegates.

questions.question: In the early eleventh century, the Chola king Rajendra I built a Shiva temple and filled it with a Sun-pedestal seized from the ______.
questions.solution:
• Origin: Chalukyas
  • Fact: Rajendra I was a great conqueror; the Sun-pedestal was a trophy of his victory over the Western Chalukyas.

questions.question: Some important administrative posts were hereditary during the Rashtrakuta and Chola dynasties. The post ‘nagara-shreshthi’ meant?
questions.solution:
• Meaning: Merchant of the city
  • Social Structure: These hereditary posts show that wealthy urban traders held significant administrative power.

questions.question: Mughal ruler, Aurangzeb died in which year?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1707
  • Significance: His death in Ahmednagar marked the beginning of the rapid decline of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian freedom fighters said that "Be the change that you wish to see in the world"?
questions.solution:
• Leader: Mahatma Gandhi
  • Philosophy: This quote emphasizes personal accountability and non-violent social transformation.

questions.question: How many types of taxes were in the reign of the ruler Alauddin Khalji?
questions.solution:
• Taxes: Three
  • Details: 1. On cultivation (Kharaj), 2. On cattle, and 3. On houses.

questions.question: Dadabhai Naoroji offered a scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule through his book entitled ‘__________’.
questions.option_2: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
questions.solution:
• Book: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
  • Theory: He introduced the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, explaining how Britain was plucking India's resources.

questions.question: In which among the following sites of Harappan civilization Jadeite stone was found?
questions.solution:
• Site: Daojali Hading
  • Location: A Neolithic site in Assam where stones (likely from China) were found, indicating ancient trade links.

questions.question: Who was considered as last powerful Mughal ruler of India?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Aurangzeb
  • Context: After him, the Mughal emperors were known as 'Later Mughals' and lacked significant central authority.

questions.question: Mirza Kamran was the brother of which Mughal emperor?
questions.solution:
• Brother: Humayun
  • Conflict: Kamran Mirza was a constant rival to Humayun, often conspiring against him for the throne of Kabul.

questions.question: In the beginning of the 19th century cotton mills in India were mostly located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
• State: Maharashtra
  • Reason: The presence of black soil (ideal for cotton) and the port of Bombay made it the industrial hub.

questions.question: Ravikirti was the court poet of which of the following dynasty ruler?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Chalukyas
  • Fact: He wrote the famous Aihole Inscription praising the victory of Pulakesin II over Harshavardhana.

questions.question:
Who said the following words?
“Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai, dekhna hai zor kitna baazu-e-qaatil me hai”
questions.solution:
• Author: Ramprasad Bismil
  • Context: A famous Urdu ghazal used as a war cry by Indian revolutionaries against British rule.

questions.question: The arms Act which disallowed Indians from having arms was passed in ______.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1878
  • Context: Passed under Lord Lytton to prevent Indians from being armed and potentially revolting.

questions.question: Ajmer became the suba headquarters under the ______.
questions.solution:
• Empire: Mughals
  • Importance: Located at the foot of the Aravalli Range, it was a strategic military and administrative center.

questions.question: The Durga temple at Aihole, built about ______ years ago.
questions.solution:
• Age: 1400 years ago (7th Century)
  • Style: It is a Chalukyan temple famous for its unique apsidal (semi-circular) shape.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers appointed two gardeners, Laddha and Pira, to high administrative posts?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Muhammad Tughlaq
  • Fact: He was criticized by contemporary chroniclers for promoting commoners to high administrative ranks.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Indian National Congress split into two groups named as Moderates and Extremists?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1907
  • Event: Known as the Surat Split; the two groups differed on methods of agitation.

questions.question: Who among the following ruler ruled before Prithviraj Chauhan over Delhi?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Ananga Pala
  • Dynasty: A Tomar Rajput king who is credited with settling Delhi in the 11th century.
